name: Thigh
overview: The Bible uses the thigh as a significant symbol in solemn oaths and covenantal commitments, as seen when Abraham commands his servant to place his hand under his thigh to swear an oath (Genesis 24:2, 9), and similarly when Jacob instructs Joseph to do the same before his death (Genesis 47:29). Additionally, the physical vulnerability of the thigh is highlighted in Jacob's wrestling encounter, where his thigh is touched and injured, leading to a lasting dietary practice among the Israelites (Genesis 32:25, 32). The thigh also represents modesty and dignity, as indicated by the instruction to cover the thighs with linen breeches in the priestly garments (Exodus 28:42). Together, these passages reveal the thigh as a locus of solemn promise, physical consequence, and respectful covering in Scripture.
